acs.text: Submitting the registration form with every field empty keeps the customer on the form and shows a message next to each required field: "First name is required.", "Last name is required.", "Address is required.", "City is required.", "State is required.", "Zip Code is required.", "Social Security Number is required.", "Username is required.", "Password is required.", "Password confirmation is required.". No message is shown for Phone #.
outcomes: the customer stays on the registration form
"First name is required." next to First Name
"Last name is required." next to Last Name
"Address is required." next to Address
"City is required." next to City
"State is required." next to State
"Zip Code is required." next to Zip Code
"Social Security Number is required." next to SSN
"Username is required." next to Username
"Password is required." next to Password
"Password confirmation is required." next to Confirm
no message is shown for Phone #

acs.text: When Password and Confirm differ, the form shows "Passwords did not match." and no customer is created (the user name cannot sign in afterwards).
outcomes: the form shows "Passwords did not match."
no customer is created: the user name cannot sign in afterwards

acs.text: A complete, valid registration opens a page with the heading Welcome <username> (source: "Welcome _<username>_") and the text "Your account was created successfully. You are now logged in." The customer is signed in: the left panel greets them with Welcome <first name> <last name> (source: "Welcome _<first name> <last name>_") and shows the Account Services menu.
outcomes: a page with the heading Welcome <username> (story: "Welcome _<username>_")
the text "Your account was created successfully. You are now logged in."
the left panel greets the customer with Welcome <first name> <last name> (story: "Welcome _<first name> <last name>_")
the left panel shows the Account Services menu

acs.text: Registering again with a user name that is already taken shows "This username already exists." next to Username and does not change the existing customer (a REST login of the existing customer still returns their original first and last name).
outcomes: "This username already exists." next to Username
a REST login of the existing customer still returns their original first and last name

acs.text: On the Customer Login panel, signing in with a wrong password shows an "Error!" page with "The username and password could not be verified."; signing in with both fields empty shows "Please enter a username and password."
outcomes: wrong password: an "Error!" page with "The username and password could not be verified."
both fields empty: "Please enter a username and password."

acs.text: Signing in with the registered user name and password opens the Accounts Overview page, which lists at least one account for the new customer. "Log Out" returns to the home page with the Customer Login panel.
outcomes: the Accounts Overview page opens
it lists at least one account for the new customer
"Log Out" returns to the home page with the Customer Login panel

acs.text: GET /login/{username}/{password} with valid credentials answers 200 and returns the customer: id, firstName, lastName, address (street, city, state, zipCode) and phoneNumber, equal to the values entered at registration. With Accept: application/json the body is JSON; without it, XML with a customer root element.
outcomes: the body contains the customer's id
firstName, lastName, address (street, city, state, zipCode) and phoneNumber equal the values entered at registration
with Accept: application/json the body is JSON
without Accept: application/json the body is XML with a customer root element

acs.text: GET /login/{username}/{password} with a wrong password answers 400 with the body "Invalid username and/or password".
outcomes: body "Invalid username and/or password"

acs.text: End to end: for a customer registered through the page, GET /customers/{id} (id from the login response) returns the same customer, and GET /customers/{id}/accounts returns the account(s) whose numbers are shown in the Accounts Overview.
outcomes: GET /customers/{id} returns the same customer as the login response
GET /customers/{id}/accounts returns the account(s) whose numbers are shown in the Accounts Overview

rules.text: Registration form fields: First Name, Last Name, Address, City, State, Zip Code, Phone #, SSN, Username, Password, Confirm. Phone # is optional; all other fields are required.
Every check starts by registering its own customer with a fresh, unique user name; the password comes from the environment variable PB_USER_PASSWORD (never hard-coded).
